doc.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Finding the right key for singers; difficult charts
summary: He sets singers' keys in workshops, and Jerry Dodgion says his music is hard until learned.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: pianist plays better in that key kind of a thing. And I’ll say well look it, let’s try this a half a step lower, a half a step higher. And they say wow, it feels much better.
Wow. They must be appreciative of that.

Do it in B, not B flat. Well I can’t, the piano player can’t play it. Well he’s going to have to learn or get somebody who can basically. Because you’re up there. Because the singer is straining. You say well — so that, believe it or not is a tremendous thing that nobody really thinks about, a lot of singers, they say well this key’s fine. And so when I do these vocal workshops that’s the first thing I do, what key do you do it in. Okay, let’s try this key, try that key. And sometimes I’ll do it with their accompanist. “I can’t.” So it’s amazing. So I mean when I deal with vocalists I deal with it on that level.
It’s good for both of them. It makes the piano player work harder.

Like I told my arranging class, even in the class, show no mercy. I mean you’re there, you’re putting your stuff out there on the line, but even as a writer you don’t write down, you never write down. You just write. And it’s the orchestra or band’s job — my music is difficult play but a friend of mine, Jerry Dodgion, a wonderful saxophonist and also has one of the greatest attitudes in the world, and is also a wonderful writer. He writes like one chart a year but it’s a good one, but he said your music is difficult, it’s difficult to play, and then when you learn it it’s great. It works. It lays great. But he said for some reason it’s difficult to play after you learn it. You say well why? Fortunately you fall in the category of when you learn it it’s fun to play but it’s hard. It’s hard music.
